tagline: A hill village that stopped changing around 1860.
intro: Route 183 turns scenic at Route 182 and runs into Colebrook center, a village in an isolated valley in the hills just south of the Massachusetts line, then goes on northwest to North Colebrook, where the designation ends at Church Hill Road. It is under four miles.

There was little land here fit for crops, so the 19th-century town raised sheep and cattle and ran tanneries on Center Brook. Since about 1860 the village has seen little change. Summer visitors are its trade now.

moments.title: Colebrook Center
moments.text: The town argued over where its center belonged until about 1790, and the 1842 Greek Revival church now stands at the south end of the triangular common.

moments.title: Colebrook Store
moments.text: Opposite the town hall stands the Federal-style store of 1812, and past the Samuel Rockwell House beyond it the village runs down to Center Brook.
